title: In vitro and in vivo evaluation of virus-induced innate immunity in mouse
protocol: Plate Vero cells into a 10 cm cell culture dish and culture in cell culture medium for 10–12 h to achieve an 80% confluent monolayer.
Wash the cells once with PBS, add 10 ml of cell culture medium to each dish, and infect cells with VSV diluted with DMEM at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.1.
Cultivate infected dishes for about 24 h at 37°C in a 5% CO2 incubator.
Observe the infected cells for cytopathic effect (CPE), when most cells display CPE, freeze the cell culture dish containing supernatant and cells directly in a -80°C freezer.
Defrost the frozen cells at 24°C–26°C.
Transfer the cell medium to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell medium at 3000 × g, 20 min at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant.
Remove about 100 μL for virus titer determination.
Store the remainder in a -80°C freezer.
Remove the 96-well plate from the incubator.
Check that the cells are in good condition.
Add virus dilutions from 10−4 to 10−11 successively to the plate, with one row for each dilution and 10 replicates in each row.
Add 90 μL DMEM without virus to the 11th and 12th wells of each row as control.
Place the 96-well plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 cell incubator for further culture.
Discard the medium in the wells after 3 days.
Add 50 μL 0.1% crystal violet stain solution to each well.
Stain the cells for 30 min at 37°C.
Observe the cells for cytopathic effect (CPE) and count CPE-positive wells.
Calculate the positive rate for each row.
Determine the virus titer by the Spearman-Karber method.
Inject each age- and sex-matched 6–12-week-old mice intraperitoneally with 0.7 mL of Brewer thioglycollate medium.
Soak the mice in 70% alcohol for 5 min.
Cut the extraperitoneal skin with sterile scissors and forceps to expose the inner skin lining the peritoneal cavity.
Inject 8 ml of cold harvest medium into the peritoneal cavity using a 10-mL syringe with a 26G needle.
Massage the abdomen of the mice for 10–20 s.
Collect peritoneal fluid containing macrophages using a 2-mL syringe.
Transfer the collected fluid to a sterile centrifuge tube on ice.
Centrifuge the peritoneal exudate cells at 400 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells with 1–2 mL red blood cell (RBC) lysis buffer per mouse, if removing erythrocytes is necessary.
Leave the cells at 24°C–26°C for 5 minutes to allow RBC lysis.
Add 5 mL of cell culture medium and centrifuge the suspension at 400 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Wash the cells with cold PBS.
Centrifuge the suspension at 400 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C to wash cells.
Discard PBS after washing.
Resuspend the peritoneal macrophages in 1 mL of cell culture medium (approx. 1 × 10^7 cells per mouse).
Count the cells and adjust their concentration to 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in cell culture medium.
Add the cell suspension to wells at a volume of 1 mL/well for a 12-well plate.
Culture the macrophages at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 1–2 hours.
Gently wash non-adherent cells with PBS after culturing.
Observe the phenotype of peritoneal macrophages by microscope.
Wash the cultured macrophages twice with PBS.
Culture the cells in DMEM and infect them with VSV, diluted with DMEM (MOI, 0.1), for 1 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Replace the medium with cell culture medium and culture for the required times at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Extract mRNA from cultured cells.
Reverse-transcribe extracted mRNA with a reverse transcription system.
Detect the expression of Ifnb1 and VSV mRNA by qPCR.
Infect age- and sex-matched 6–12-week-old mice with VSV (2 × 10^8 PFU/mouse) by intraperitoneal injection.
Euthanize the infected mice 24 h later according to approved methods.
Allow blood samples to clot for 2 h at 24°C–26°C and then centrifuge for 20 min at 2000 × g at 4°C.
Collect serum and assay immediately, or aliquot and store samples at -80°C.
Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles of stored serum.
Collect mouse lung, spleen, and liver and cut into small pieces for further analysis.
Prepare fresh tissue pieces and place them in 1.5-mL tubes.
Quickly freeze the samples with liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen samples at −80°C for up to 6 months.
Homogenize lung, spleen, and liver tissues in TRIzol or DMEM.
Centrifuge the homogenized tissue mixture at 400 × g for 8 minutes at 4°C.
Extract RNA from the lung tissue using TRIzol or an equivalent method.
Convert extracted RNA to cDNA using a reverse transcription system.
Analyze Ifnb1 and VSV mRNA expression by qPCR.
Determine VSV titer in homogenized lung tissue supernatant by TCID50 assay.
Measure IFN-β concentrations in mouse serum using a mouse IFN-β ELISA kit.
Place lung tissues in tissue processing embedding cassettes.
Immerse tissues in 4% paraformaldehyde for 1 hour.
Incubate tissues in 70% ethanol for 2 hours (I).
Incubate tissues in 70% ethanol for 2 hours (II).
Incubate tissues in 80% ethanol for 30 minutes.
Incubate tissues in 90% ethanol for 30 minutes.
Incubate tissues in 95% ethanol for 30 minutes (I).
Incubate tissues in 95% ethanol for 2 hours (II).
Incubate tissues in anhydrous ethanol for 40 minutes (I).
Incubate tissues in anhydrous ethanol for 30 minutes (II).
Incubate tissues in xylene for 20 minutes (I).
Incubate tissues in xylene for 35 minutes (II).
Immerse tissues in paraffin for 12 hours.
Embed tissues in paraffin using an embedding machine.
Cut 5-μm lung tissue sections using a microtome.
Deparaffinize paraffin sections by placing them in xylene for 2 × 10 min (blot excess xylene before transferring).
Transfer sections to anhydrous ethanol and incubate for 2 × 5 min.
Rehydrate the sections with 95% ethanol for 10 min.
Further rehydration occurs when placed in 80% ethanol for 10 min.
Rinse paraffin sections in distilled water for 5 min.
Apply hematoxylin to lung tissue using a pipette and stain for 2–3 min.
Rinse the stained section in running tap water for 5 min.
Differentiate with 0.5% acid alcohol for 1–3 s.
Rinse well in tap water for 5 min.
Rinse sections in deionized water for 5 min.
Counterstain tissue in eosin for 4-5 minutes.
Dehydrate the tissue by incubating in 80% ethanol for 3 seconds.
Transfer to anhydrous ethanol and incubate for 3 seconds.
Further dehydration occurs when placed in anhydrous ethanol for 2 × 10 min (blot excess ethanol before transferring).
Incubate sections in xylene for 2 × 10 min.
Place a coverslip on the slide using neutral balsam.
Apply a drop of neutral balsam to the slide, angle the coverslip and let it fall gently onto the slide, ensuring no bubbles remain beneath the tissue.
Allow the neutral balsam to spread under the coverslip covering the entire tissue section.
Observe stained lung sections with a light microscope.
Photograph observed tissue sections for documentation.
